page.overview:
What is The Lord of the Rings?

The Lord of the Rings is J.R.R. Tolkien's epic of Frodo Baggins, the Fellowship, and the quest to destroy the One Ring forged by Sauron in Mordor.

entity.description:
The Lord of the Rings is an epic high fantasy novel written by J.R.R. Tolkien, which was later fitted as a trilogy. The story began as a sequel to Tolkien's earlier fantasy book , and soon developed into a much larger story. At publication, it was divided into (1954), (1955), and (1955). Around 1968, one-volume editions started to be published in both hardcover and paperback, but both those editions are now exceedingly rare.

Written in stages between 1937 and 1949, with much of it during World War II, it was originally published in three volumes in 1954 and 1955. It has since been reprinted numerous times and translated into at least 38 different languages, becoming one of the most popular works of twentieth-century literature.

The action in The Lord of the Rings is set in what the author conceived to be the lands of the real Earth, inhabited by humanity but placed in a fictional past, before familiar history but after the fall of his version of Atlantis, Númenor. Tolkien gave this setting a modern English name, Middle-earth, a rendering of the Old English Middangeard.

The story concerns peoples such as Hobbits, Elves, Men, Dwarves, Wizards, and Orcs (called goblins in The Hobbit), and centers on the Ring of Power made by the Dark Lord Sauron. Starting from quiet beginnings in the Shire, the story ranges across Middle-earth and follows the courses of the War of the Ring. The main story is followed by six appendices that provide a wealth of historical and linguistic background material, as well as an index listing every character, place, song, and sword.
